title: Combinator-like symbolic rewriting systems can behave randomly

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Combinator-like symbolic rewriting systems can behave randomly

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Symbolic systems that repeatedly apply a single rewrite rule of the form e[x_][y_] → (expression in x and y) to nested expressions can, like other simple programs, produce behavior that is complex and seemingly random rather than stabilizing.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 3: The World of Simple Programs

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But often—just as in so many other kinds of systems—the behavior is instead complex and seemingly quite random.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 3, “The World of Simple Programs”; section “Symbolic Systems” (from p. 102), p. 104. Scope: combinator-like symbolic expression rewriting systems

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch03-17: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.80

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The systems are precisely executable and bounded rule spaces can be enumerated with standard software. Existing computation can demonstrate many examples, but cannot establish unrestricted randomness or a rule-independent frequency without additional conventions.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Enumerate bounded rewrite expressions and seeds, iterate each for a fixed horizon, and classify stabilization, periodicity, growth, compressibility, and statistical irregularity. Reproducible non-stabilizing, low-compressibility cases confirm existence, while frequencies quantify the word often.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Apparent randomness is test-relative rather than a mathematically decisive property.

Nontermination and long transients limit exhaustive classification.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.9
analysis feasibility: 0.88
operationalizability: 0.72
data adequacy: 0.72
discriminating power: 0.78

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim is an existence claim about a fully specified class of rewrite systems, and both the rules in the book and a wider sample of short rules can be rerun exactly. Non-stabilizing growth together with a failed periodicity check is a direct confirming outcome, and universal stabilization in the searched class would refute it. The only soft spot is how strongly a finite sample supports 'often,' which is not required to settle the stated 'can.'

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Enumerate small combinator-style rules of the form e[x_][y_] to an expression in x and y, iterate them from a fixed seed, and record whether expression size stabilizes, becomes periodic or nested, or keeps growing while passing randomness tests. A single non-stabilizing, statistically irregular example confirms the claim; every small rule stabilizing or becoming nested would refute it inside that rule bound.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Visual or statistical irregularity does not prove that a particular rule never eventually stabilizes.

The frequency word 'often' depends on how the space of expressions is enumerated.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.7
data existence: 0.85
data adequacy: 0.75
discriminating power: 0.7
